conviction_note: The print date is confirmed (WSH CON plus the issuer's own 2026-09-29 notice: Q3 ended 2026-08-28, release after the close on 2026-10-07, call 2026-10-08 08:30 ET). No single fact decides this print. The findings sum to -1.0: management's own seasonal-softness guide (about 8% lost production), tariff input-cost inflation against a record 36.5% Q2 gross margin, and a 26% 20-day run-up into a name whose last two record-ish prints sold off. Against that sit an FX tailwind (Q3 average USD/CAD about 1.40 against 1.373 in Q2) and defence deliveries starting, read through TTM's +14% A&D. The scaled number is p_up 45 on a 5.5% scale, so -0.55. It is smaller than the sum because the bar comes from one aggregator, and because my EPS estimate (about 0.16-0.17 against 0.18) rests on my own margin arithmetic, not on a document. The auditor change to Deloitte (McGovern Hurley resigned at FTG's request on 2026-08-12, no reportable event) was read and has no bearing on this print.

findings.finding: Management pre-guided Q3 (Jun-Aug) as seasonally softer, with about one week or 8% of production lost. On the Q2 run-rate of C$52.7M that implies roughly C$48.5M before growth, FX and defence ramp. Against a C$0.18 EPS bar (Q2 printed 0.20, Q3-25 0.11), my arithmetic (about C$50-51M revenue, about 34% GM, opex near Q2) gives EPS of about 0.15-0.17, and revenue below the snippet-only C$53M average.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (adj EBITDA down YoY despite +10% revenue): -10.89% (baseline, 2026-04-09). Q2 2026 record EPS 0.20 against a 0.16 bar: -3.03% (baseline, 2026-07-08). Q4 2025 (EPS 0.14 against 0.13): +6.71%.
findings.why_not_priced: With two analysts and a single aggregator estimate, nobody publishes a quarter model the market can see. The visible EPS bar (0.18) sits only 10% under Q2's record 0.20, while the guided 8% production loss plus normal absorption leverage points lower. If the softness were priced, the stock would not be up 26% in 20 sessions and near its high into the print.
findings.independence: Q3-25 printed C$47.7M against C$48.7M in Q2-25, a seasonal dip shown in the Q2 2026 MD&A quarterly table (https://app.quotemedia.com/data/downloadFiling?webmasterId=101020&ref=6a4ebf481444bd3fff03dd02&type=PDFC&symbol=FTG%3ACA&companyName=Firan+Technology+Group+Corporation&formType=002-002-001097-001004&formDescription=MD%26A&dateFiled=2026-07-08). The EPS bar itself is one source.

findings.finding: The Canadian dollar was weaker through FTG's Q3. Bank of Canada USD/CAD averaged 1.404 in June, 1.411 in July and about 1.39 in August, against a Q2 average of 1.373 and a Q3-25 average of 1.372. That lifts CAD-reported revenue about 2% on a business with roughly 90% non-Canadian sales, and widens margin at the Canadian plants, which sell in USD with CAD costs. The period-end rate (about 1.387 on 08-28 against 1.380 on 05-29) also implies a small revaluation gain rather than Q2's C$0.3M loss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX was a named headwind in Q1 2026 (C$1.3M revenue, C$0.7M FX loss in Circuits), and that print fell -10.89%. In Q2 FX was a smaller drag and the print fell -3.03%. There is no clean history of an FX-tailwind quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: analysts can see the rate. FTG hedges by selling USD forward, so the realised gain is diluted (Q2 hedge loss in revenue: C$0.23M), and the size reaching the P&L is uncertain. It is a proxy, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The company's own MD&A states that most sales are in USD and a significant share of costs is in CAD (Q2 MD&A, p.10, same filing URL as finding 1). The rate data is independent of the company.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call the CEO said tariffs are now raising Circuits input costs, 'in the millions of dollars in 2026', with input costs 'moving up fast' and pass-through to customers only started. So Q2's record 36.5% gross margin (36.7% before FX) is unlikely to hold in a lower-volume Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 Circuits adj EBITDA fell from C$5.5M to C$4.0M on margin; the stock fell -10.89%. Q2 GM jumped to 36.5%, yet the stock still fell -3.03%.
findings.why_not_priced: The cost warning was qualitative and came on the same call as a record margin quarter. The C$0.18 bar, at 90% of Q2's EPS on lower volume, implies near-record margins persisting. Had the market priced margin normalisation, consensus would sit nearer the Q3-25-style seasonal ratio.
findings.independence: Same transcript as finding 1 (one document, two separate facts: volume and unit cost). The Q2 MD&A tariff paragraph (p.15, same filing URL) independently states 'increased input costs, due to tariffs on raw materials'.

findings.finding: Initial deliveries on the two classified defence PCB programs (CEO: C$50-100M a year of customer board spend in total) were scheduled to begin in Q3 2026, and opening POs are in a record C$193.5M backlog (book-to-bill 1.64). TTM Technologies' Q2 (quarter to 2026-06-29) showed A&D sales +14% YoY, a 1.49 company book-to-bill and a raised outlook, so bookings and backlog are likely strong again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 record bookings (+89%) and backlog (+30%): -3.03%. The backlog line has not been rewarded on the print day.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the programs and their Q3 start were disclosed in Q1 and Q2 and the stock is up 112% YTD. What is unpriced is the size of the first deliveries and any program-award commentary, since backlog includes only POs and not awards. It is a proxy read-through, sized small.
findings.independence: FTG's own Q2 release (https://www.globenewswire.com/ via TMX newsid 5621509566118205; mirrored at https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/press-releases/2026/07/10/firan-technology-group-corporation-ftg-announces-second-quarter-2026-financial-results/) states that initial deliveries are expected starting Q3 2026.

findings.finding: US 50% Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods took effect 2026-08-19, regardless of USMCA origin, with qualifying civil aircraft and parts exempt. On 2026-08-24 Canadian aerospace sold off (FTG -13.9% on 237k shares, Magellan -8.5%, TMX tape), and FTG has since fully recovered (18.76 to 24.80). The Q3 call is the first time the company comments on its exposure after the effective date, especially for Toronto-made PCBs, which may not count as 'aircraft parts'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-08-24 tariff-scare day: -13.9% with no company news, then a full recovery by late September.
findings.why_not_priced: The full recovery says the market has decided FTG is exempt or immaterial. If the company says Toronto Circuits exports are caught, that decision is wrong; if it confirms the exemption, there is little left to gain. Scope is unconfirmed: this is macro-to-company transmission, so it is sized small and close to zero.
findings.independence: Magellan's same-day -8.5% on the TMX tape (getCompanyPriceHistory MAL, 2026-08-21 to 08-24) points to a sector move, not FTG-specific news. FTG's MD&A says nearly all North American products comply with USMCA, which this tariff ignores.

Short interest is only 1.28% (2.7 days to cover). This is a name whose two most recent prints were sold even on records.

findings.why_not_priced: This is largely the free control (-run_up_20d) wearing a hat, so it is sized small. What it adds is the observed reaction function: this holder base has sold the last two prints regardless of quality.

outside_window.finding: US Section 232 aerospace proclamation of 2026-07-09: no tariffs now, a 180-day negotiation window ending around early January 2027, tariffs reserved. Separately, US tariffs on Canadian autos and steel step up to 50% on 2027-01-01.
